doc.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016

title: The Fender Rhodes: a 73 suitcase model, its mechanics and sound
summary: Rydin liked the Rhodes sound but not its mechanics, added wheels, tuned it himself, and finally sold it for more than he paid.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And you used a Fender Rhodes?

Yes, in the 70s I did and in the 80s yes. In fact I liked it, I still like the sound of it but it has terrible mechanics. It’s not so nice to play on. But I do like the sound. But if I was Herbie Hancock and someone or other brought it for me — but it’s I mean, bringing this heavy to a gig and you are like that, and then afterwards you have to take it home. So I got tired of it. So after I think like 25 years I sold it and I got more money selling it than I bought it in the early 70s.
Did you have the suitcase model? Or the 88?
No I had the 73 suitcase. The first thing I did is I put wheels on it so that indoors I could use it, and I put metal all over, in the corners.
And did you learn how to tune it yourself?

Yes. And you can do a lot with the sound, with how to put the microphones next to it and you can get different sounds if it’s like that or if it’s like that. And you can also change the mechanics a little. It’s still not very good mechanics.
